added_lemmas.justification: A support-level condition, rather than a hand-picked matrix, certifies a universally valid nonpartition design with a matching global power upper bound.
added_lemmas.gap: A partition must isolate any vertex having no mutual off-diagonal neighbor, whereas a legal one-way outgoing edge can still carry resampling mass in a universally valid row kernel.
added_lemmas.consumer: An empirical legal fiber can be screened for the asymmetric-isolate pattern before running the full mixed-integer optimizer.

prose_updates.tldr: A finite conditional randomization law need not resample from a partition cell. Universal validity of an arbitrary legal row kernel is characterized exactly by the inequalities \(d_K(A)\geq\pi(A)\), with an equivalent peeling core, an \(O(m2^m)\) separator, and a finite union-of-polyhedra design region. A generic asymmetric-isolate support criterion constructs a valid nonpartition kernel with power \(\pi(x)=\alpha\) against zero for every legal partition kernel; every one-way three-cycle support is a corollary, and the original cyclic matrix remains an exact \(2/3\)-power stress test. On a predeclared network-exposure fiber, finite weak-order enumeration with strict-cell linear feasibility computes every worst-case bounded-null value and its optimizing schedule, and nested inversion gives simultaneous lower bounds for all exposure-specific effect quantiles. This exact network reduction does not reproduce the adjusted-outcome computations of Caughey--Dafoe--Li--Miratrix or Su--Li; a two-unit example gives frozen and comparator values \(1\) and \(1/2\), respectively.

project_justification.fill: The project gives exact row-kernel validity geometry, a generic asymmetric-isolate support certificate with a strict partition power gap, the uniform three-cycle as a finite stress-test corollary, certified catalogue-power design, a terminating exact weak-order and linear-feasibility reduction for bounded-null schedules, and simultaneous within-exposure quantile projection. It also gives an explicit obstruction to claiming exact recovery of the Caughey or Su--Li computational statistics.

prose_updates.related_work: Zhang and Zhao (2023) formulate conditional randomization through assignment-space partitions and prove validity by a conditional probability-integral transform; their partition kernel is strictly contained in the score-uniform row-kernel characterization. The asymmetric-isolate proposition makes the separation support-theoretic: a partition must singletonize a vertex with no mutual off-diagonal neighbor, while a one-way legal edge from that vertex yields a valid kernel attaining the universal level bound. The directed three-cycle is a finite corollary and stress test, not the limit of the construction. Ramdas et al. (2023) validate arbitrary nonuniform permutation laws after a random reference permutation restores exchangeability, a different construction from an unmodified deterministic row kernel. Puelz et al. (2022) encode imputability through null-exposure graphs and bicliques, which supply legal network fibers, while Yanagi and Sei (2022) use an approximate model-based power expression to refine biclique selection. Caughey et al. (2023, Theorem 4 and Section 5.5) provide individual and simultaneous no-interference effect-quantile inference under exchangeable treatment, and Su and Li (2024) provide stratified quantile tests and a multiple-choice-knapsack computation. Their order-statistic null equivalence and inversion logic inform the present construction, but the frozen score evaluates assignment-specific imputed outcomes rather than a fixed adjusted-outcome vector; the explicit two-unit witness therefore rules out exact computational recovery of either method. Chen and Li's 2026 finite-sample improvements likewise concern no-interference complete, stratified, sampling-based, or matched designs. Owusu (2023) studies network heterogeneous-effect randomization tests with adaptive focal assignments; the Cai, de Janvry, and Sadoulet weather-insurance reanalysis is the intended empirical consumer, not evidence for the theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The universal iff, recursion, peeling equivalence, polyhedral representation, finite kernel optimizer, generic asymmetric-isolate power certificate, strict three-state inclusion and power witness, minimal coupled pattern, and composite-null validity are theorem-level results. The asymmetric-isolate family proves a strict partition gap whenever the stated support pattern occurs; it does not assert that an actual Cai--Owusu fiber has that pattern or a positive optimized gap. The network schedule problem is closed by finite weak-order enumeration and strict-cell linear feasibility; for nonempty null schedule sets it returns an optimizing schedule, while empty sets are certified infeasible. Nested inversion yields exact simultaneous lower bounds for all effect quantiles at one predeclared exposure, including the empty-region convention through finite-cell stabilization. The no-interference count null is exactly an order-statistic null and partition kernels remain valid, but the frozen assignment-specific score does not equal the Caughey adjusted-outcome statistic or the Su--Li knapsack statistic, so neither algorithm is claimed as an exact specialization. Cross-exposure simultaneity and an actual Cai--Owusu power gain remain outside the theorem and require, respectively, explicit level allocation and empirical fiber computation. Ordinary exact computation assumes rational or real-algebraic input representations; arbitrary real constants are covered only in an ideal exact-real-arithmetic model.

statement_notes.gap: Partition and biclique kernels cannot use a one-way outgoing comparison from a vertex having no mutual off-diagonal neighbor, because legal conditioning forces that vertex into a singleton cell; the asymmetric-isolate proposition turns this support obstruction into a strict power gap.
statement_notes.consumer: Before enumerating all partitions on a Cai--Owusu exposure fiber, screen its legal support for an asymmetric-isolate vertex; the directed three-cycle remains a minimal unit test.

statement_notes.gap: Yanagi and Sei (2022) optimize an approximate criterion within biclique constructions, whereas the mixed-integer program optimizes exact rejection probability over all universally valid legal row kernels; the asymmetric-isolate family supplies an analytic instance with a matching global upper bound.
statement_notes.consumer: The Cai weather-insurance reanalysis can first test for the analytic asymmetric-isolate certificate and then compare the globally optimized kernel with every partition kernel at the prespecified level.

statement_notes.justification: The uniform directed cycle is the smallest exhaustive stress test for the broader asymmetric-isolate support mechanism and also exhibits a sharper \(2/3\)-power cyclic kernel at its stated score and level.
statement_notes.gap: Partition kernels cannot use any one-way edge on this support; the generic asymmetric-isolate construction needs only one such edge, while the displayed cyclic kernel uses all three to reach power \(2/3\).
statement_notes.consumer: The Cai weather-insurance presolve can use the three-state calculation as a unit test and the asymmetric-isolate criterion as a support-level screening rule before full optimization.

statement_notes.gap: The no-interference comparator boundary supplies the order-statistic interpretation of the count null and finite-sample validity under complete or stratified partition randomization, but the frozen assignment-specific score differs from the Caughey adjusted-outcome and Su--Li statistics.
statement_notes.consumer: Use the comparator results to validate null interpretation and coverage, but do not reuse their adjusted-outcome or multiple-choice-knapsack routines to compute the frozen schedule score.
